clue.text: Is harrowing about it in literary work

indicators.note: one word going about another wraps round it, so the second sits inside the first

parts.note: harrows or torments, as in wrings someone's heart

explanation.surface: Something distressing hidden somewhere in a work of literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is harrowing' reads as an adjective in the surface, but it is a verb phrase: wrings as in wrings the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Writings are the collected texts an author produces, so a body of literary output.

clue.text: Sources of any largely uncommon metal provide metallic salt

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so each following word yields its opening letter

parts.note: initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Rare metals supplying a salt used in chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: Alum is a double sulphate of aluminium and potassium, a classic crystalline salt containing metal.

clue.text: Persistent hanger-on exhausted visitor from far away?

explanation.surface: A clingy guest who has worn themselves out after travelling a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the far-away visitor is an alien, ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet is a mollusc that clings to rocks, and figuratively a person who stubbornly attaches themselves to others.

clue.text: Reminder to look up when taking drink in Japan

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look

explanation.surface: A traveller in Japan glancing up from a cup of rice wine to recall something.
explanation.walkthrough: PEEK read upwards is KEEP, followed by SAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a small object kept to remind its owner of a person or occasion.

clue.text: Rectories, I fancy, may be location of 12

indicators.note: used as a verb of imagining, it invites us to picture these letters in a new form

explanation.surface: Imagining that vicarages are where you might find a pot of ink.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is INKPOT; an escritoire is where you would keep one.
explanation.definitionFit: An escritoire is a writing desk with compartments, the natural place to keep an inkpot.

clue.text: Stretch of water's about devoid of life, mostly after introduction of sulphur

indicators.note: introducing something puts it inside, so a letter is slipped into the shortened word
most of a word but not all of it, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A body of water described as lifeless once sulphur has got into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at the Dead Sea, but devoid of life only supplies letters; the sulphur goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Sea is the inlet of the Indian Ocean between Africa and Arabia, a named stretch of water.

clue.text: One avoiding heat rests — these may act as sunshades

indicators.note: the word for heat steers clear of the numeral, so that letter is left out

parts.note: to broil is to heat fiercely

explanation.surface: Someone escaping the hot sun lounges about with protection overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: BROIL minus I is BROL, then LIES. Brolly is British slang for an umbrella.
explanation.definitionFit: Brollies are umbrellas, which keep off rain but can equally be held up to block strong sun.

clue.text: Stone on dress flashing in light

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for the stone weight

explanation.surface: A gem sewn onto a gown sparkling in the light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' works because this is a down entry: the first piece sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe is a lamp that produces rapid regular flashes, so it describes light that flickers on and off.

clue.text: Followed English and American backing, in conclusion

indicators.note: the reversed pair is placed inside the word that follows
backing means moving in the opposite direction, so the pair is read from right to left

explanation.surface: British and American sides agreeing in the end, as happened next.
explanation.walkthrough: Both abbreviations are reversed together, not just the American one, before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensued means came afterwards or resulted, the same as followed in the sense of happening next.

clue.text: Nothing in money supply? A very small amount

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

explanation.surface: An empty cash machine leaving the customer with next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money supply' looks like economics jargon but is a cash machine, an ATM.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the tiniest particle, and figuratively a minute quantity, as in not an atom of sense.

clue.text: Works appear rash, to put things another way

indicators.note: to work material is to knead and shape it, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone's output seems hasty when they try rephrasing.
explanation.definitionFit: To paraphrase is to restate a passage in different words while keeping its meaning.

clue.text: Contribution to 1, say, left out connection with drug

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left is omitted from the word for connection

explanation.surface: Something that helped a piece of writing, missing a link to a narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 is WRITINGS: an inkpot supplies the ink that produces them. LINK loses L to give INK, then POT.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkpot holds the ink a writer dips into, so it is one thing that contributes to written work.

clue.text: Player in old plays missing climax from tricksy Italian playwright

indicators.note: letters that play about move freely into another order
the phrase lacks that letter, so it is removed before rearranging
the climax of a word comes at its end, so only its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: An actor in old dramas by a clever, mischievous Italian dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player in old plays' reads like a description of an actor, but 'plays' is the anagram signal: Y comes out of PLAYER IN OLD and the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Pirandello was the Italian dramatist of Six Characters in Search of an Author and a Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Describing leaves: couple mostly greenish-blue

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: a pair, as of game birds

explanation.surface: Two items with blue-green foliage being described.
explanation.walkthrough: BRACE drops its E to give BRAC, then TEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracteal is the adjective from bract, the modified leaf at the base of a flower, so it describes such leaves.

clue.text: Urban conditions perhaps not experienced in small place

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

explanation.surface: City living being something a small-town dweller has never known.
explanation.walkthrough: PL is the street-sign abbreviation for Place.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban sprawl is the unplanned spread of a city into surrounding country, one example of urban conditions.

clue.text: Take away sense over hospital? Part of it goes into reverse

indicators.note: moving in reverse means running backwards, so the letters are read the other way

parts.note: a ward is part of a hospital

explanation.surface: A query about removing reason from a hospital, with part of the building backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' points back to hospital, so the part is WARD, which reads backwards as DRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw is to remove or take something back, as in withdrawing troops or an offer.

clue.text: Stamp involving small US state in a row

indicators.note: to involve is to enfold, so the second item is taken inside the first

explanation.surface: A postage stamp from a tiny American state, part of a set laid out in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Serial describes things arranged or happening one after another, in a series or sequence.

clue.text: Left pig covered in pig fat

indicators.note: something covered in a substance is wrapped by it, so it goes inside

explanation.surface: A pig left smeared with its own kind's fat.
explanation.walkthrough: Larboard is the old naval word for the port side, later dropped because it sounded too like starboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the archaic term for the port side of a ship, the left when facing forward.

clue.text: Latin praise? Attempt to keep Latin manner up

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within, so a letter sits inside
in a down entry, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: an air is a manner or bearing

explanation.surface: Wondering about praise in Latin while trying to keep a classical style going.
explanation.walkthrough: Latin appears twice: first in the definition, then as the abbreviation L kept inside the attempt. Only the manner is turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloria is Latin for glory, and the Gloria is the hymn of praise in the Mass; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Gas in any way curtailed about newborns

indicators.note: cutting off the tail removes the final letter of the phrase

parts.note: at all, in any way whatever

explanation.surface: A gas being cut short somehow in a baby ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In any way' stands for the phrase at all, as in not at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Neonatal means relating to newly born infants, as in neonatal care.

clue.text: Picked up hot hint about a Parisian castrato?

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting the letters up means reading them from bottom to top
a word going about another wraps round it

explanation.surface: Someone overhearing a heated tip about a French singer with an unusually high voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' suggests hearing a sound, but in a down entry it means the letters are lifted and read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrato was a singer castrated before puberty, so he is a kind of eunuch; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: I go astray in South American mountain range

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: to wander from the right path

explanation.surface: A hiker getting lost in the Andes.
explanation.walkthrough: South American is read as its abbreviation, SA, which wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged chain of mountains, the Spanish word used for ranges like the Sierra Nevada.

clue.text: A dessert's served up in layers

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the 's makes the dessert, a tart, take an S

explanation.surface: A pudding arriving in tiers, like a trifle.
explanation.walkthrough: A TARTS read upwards gives STRATA.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are the distinct horizontal layers of rock or of anything stratified, such as social classes.

clue.text: Breeder, Frenchman perhaps, taken aback about sex

indicators.note: going about another word means wrapping round it
taken aback suggests being pushed backwards, so the name is read right to left

parts.note: sex in the sense of male or female

explanation.surface: A French stud farmer startled by a discussion of sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' in the surface means startled; René stands for any Frenchman, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: An engenderer is one who engenders, that is begets or brings into being, which is what a breeder does.

clue.text: Novice reflected? That's a good thing

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: slang for a beginner, especially in gaming

explanation.surface: A beginner musing on whether their inexperience is actually an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or benefit, something helpful that one is grateful for.

clue.text: Scientist, foremost among best of historical researchers

indicators.note: the foremost part of each word is its first letter, so only the leaders are taken

parts.note: initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A scientist ranked first among the finest historians of research.
explanation.definitionFit: Niels Bohr was the Danish physicist who modelled the atom and won the Nobel Prize in Physics.

clue.text: Italian monster, namely, reverse of friend

parts.note: abbreviation of scilicet, Latin for namely

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word written backwards

explanation.surface: A monster defined as the opposite of a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is a dictionary abbreviation for namely; ALLY written backwards follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scylla was the sea monster of Greek myth living on a rock in the Strait of Messina, off Italy.

clue.text: Broadcasting on air with the dubious leading figure

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters things widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A shady presenter fronting a radio or television show.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central character lacking heroic virtues, so a protagonist of questionable morals.
